speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how long will the SGUnited Traineeship programme be available for; and (b) between ensuring adequate scrutiny and efficient processing of SGUnited Traineeship applications, how many full-time equivalent staff does the Singapore Business Federation currently have and is projecting to hire and train in the next six to 12 months so as to shorten processing time to help jobseekers and graduates start work sooner since they have found employers keen to hire them.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Manpower since the set-up of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres (a) how many Singaporeans have sought assistance at the centres; (b) how many successful job and traineeship matches have been made; and (c) how many training and skills placements have been made.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The National Jobs Council is coordinating efforts to provide job, traineeship, attachment as well as training opportunities for jobseekers under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The SGUnited Traineeships and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programmes were introduced to provide company-hosted traineeship and attachment opportunities for recent graduates and mid-career jobseekers respectively.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These programmes aim to help jobseekers who are unable to find permanent jobs in the current job market, gain industry-relevant skills and build professional networks so as to boost their employability.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The SGUnited Traineeships Programme was launched on 1 June 2020, and the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme, on 1 August 2020.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Workforce Singapore and its programme manager, the Singapore Business Federation or SBF, have worked closely with host companies to open up earlier-approved traineeship positions as company attachments for mid-career individuals under the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme as well.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The top five sectors which together account for more than half the openings are: financial services, infocomm technology and media, professional services, wholesale trade and electronics.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although the focus must now be for the host companies to secure more successful placements, SBF continues to accept new applications by companies to host attachments for mid-career individuals that commence before 31 March 2021.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I had earlier updated the House that SBF undertakes a rigorous screening process and scrutinises each application to ensure that host organisations structure their traineeships and attachments appropriately with clear development plans, so that participants can have a positive and meaningful experience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: How quickly an employer's application is approved depends in part on the comprehensiveness of its submission.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Factoring in time for SBF to seek clarifications and enhancement, most applications are approved within four weeks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is, however, not a key bottleneck right now as there are already many existing openings available to jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: After suitable matches are found and necessary supporting documents are submitted to SBF, the traineeship or company attachment can commence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To help our local jobseekers access the available jobs and skills opportunities, we have brought career matching services closer to the heartlands.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have launched the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres in phases.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Since early July and by end-August, one had been set up across all 24 HDB towns.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although all satellite career centres were only in operation from end-August, Career Ambassadors have advised about 4,200 jobseekers by now.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Jobseekers are reached through multiple channels and assisted through a variety of means.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is therefore more useful to consider their collective impact.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Between January and August this year, we have provided career matching services to about 44,200 jobseekers through the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres as well as WSG and NTUC's e2i's five permanent career centres.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is in spite of a two-month lockdown and the deep economic recession.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to curate more opportunities while seeking to increase placements of jobseekers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: My concern is about the resourcing to process the number of opportunities available.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I think it is heartening that there are many opportunities available, but given the 25 staff at SBF right now, processing over a thousand host organisations base on the statistics, that is about 40 host organisations per SBF staff.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, would the Minister not agree that for those who have lost their jobs and everyone in the family has lost their jobs, we would need to increase or a ramping up of resourcing and expedited channel to help them access these job opportunities as soon as possible?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Would the Minister consider creating a priority or fast-track channel for trainee applicants under the traineeship programmes whose families have no other working or income earning individuals?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the beginning, SBF did encounter quite a lot of difficulties because it had responded to the opportunity to curate, to manage the SGUnited Traineeship programmes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It wanted very much to be of service to their members – meaning the companies that potentially can host these opportunities – as well as to jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I would acknowledge that in the earlier stages, it did take SBF quite a while to assemble the team and to process the applications from the host companies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would also say that because the programme was very new at the time, what constitutes a meaningful traineeship experience, was something that was still being worked out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But, I am glad to say that by now, all these kinks have been ironed out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SBF certainly expanded their team and, as I had mentioned earlier in my reply, it will be at full strength by the end of this month.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Right now, if you look at the total number of opportunities that have been made available, I think that period is past.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Right now, the focus has to be on the companies making these opportunities available to jobseekers, letting the jobseekers know that they are interested to take in people as trainees or as mid-career attachments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Right now, the action is less on SBF and more on the companies to get this done.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is within the companies, their own HR teams that have to follow through with the approved positions, advertise the positions, collate the CVs, the interest that have been made known to them through various sources, and then, arrange for the interviews to take place as well as to make the selection and then follow through with SBF.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, right now, a lot of the action has to be undertaken by the host companies, themselves.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should also add another point to Ms Carrie Tan's concern.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SBF is one of the many partners that we work with.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not the only one that is involved in this whole network that is trying to bring together jobseekers as well as companies that still have openings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The whole network of Career Centres, including the 24 in the HDB Towns that I mentioned earlier in my reply, are also involved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you add all of them together, the resourcing has increased quite considerably.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The next step as to whether the job matching can happen is no longer just a matter of facilitation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The jobseeker must feel that he wants the job; the employer must feel that he can give the jobseeker an opportunity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And that is not something that you bring about purely through more facilitation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although, I will give the Member the assurance that if more resources are needed in that regard, certainly, we have no hesitation to enhance them.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I just want to ask whether we are thinking ahead, now that many of them have secured traineeships; what is the next step for them?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Are we also encouraging the companies to convert these traineeships into permanent jobs?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Would MOM also do some early survey to find out from companies how many of the trainees would be retained as permanent employees and how many may be released, so that they can better plan the next stage of helping the young graduates?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Indeed, we are following up closely with the companies to have a sense of what they are thinking of for the future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would say that if you look at the range of opportunities that have been made available, quite clearly, a lot of the companies are looking ahead into the future and seeing that this is a good time to expose more jobseekers to their industries or to the jobs that previously were perhaps less well sought after by the jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, they do have that objective in mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to whether they can follow through to offer the trainees a specific job, an opening, probably will depend on two things: one, whether they see a need to fulfil that position on a permanent basis and that will depend on their assessment of the business outlook; second, I think they will also assess the specific trainee, whether during this period, the trainee has exhibited good ability to gel with the team as well as to contribute to the organisation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is what, we think, will potentially encourage the employers to think in that direction.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have quite a number of non PMET residents who are seeking jobs but find that most of the jobs matched by SGUnited's Jobs Programmes, including the traineeships, seem to be targeted more at PMETs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the satellite Career Centres, as is the case for all the other touchpoints we have with jobseekers, all these jobs can be made available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For some of the non PMET jobseekers, we understand, for example, language may be a barrier.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, even in these career-resourcing centres, there are colleagues who speak Mandarin or speak other languages that will be of help to these jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our experience is that matching people into PMET jobs takes longer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The reason is very simple: if you are a PMET, you see yourself as having a set of skills that you would like to find the best match for in an employer that recognises your experience and is also able to pay a premium for those skills that you have.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has actually been easier to match people in non PMET roles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not have the numbers offhand, but I can assure you that the matching for non PMET has actually been the majority of those under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.
